claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified now on a constrained basis despite a remaining clinical coding assistant weakness, because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and residual risk can be managed through mitigation and monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows no material weakness remains or shows an approved mitigation satisfying all required fields.
Use noncompliant if the available evidence shows certification is being advanced without the required disclosure or without an approved mitigation.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal results are supportive but not sufficient when a specific policy predicate for disclosure or mitigation remains unmet.
Public governance guidance may support monitoring practices but cannot replace the governing internal certification requirement.
evidence_requests: Approved mitigation record for the clinical coding assistant issue showing owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Evidence of approved risk acceptance, if the issue is being treated as unresolved but accepted for launch.
Final model card or equivalent disclosure artifact showing the material limitation is disclosed for the named launch use case, or evidence that the issue is no longer material.
Underlying evidence establishing whether the observation-status coding weakness is materially significant for launch use.
specific_concerns: The available summary indicates a current unresolved weakness in a named launch use case: the clinical coding assistant observation-status coding slice remains below target.
The draft mitigation runbook is incomplete because the owner and alert threshold are still marked TBD, so the mitigation does not meet the stated policy standard for an approved mitigation.
The policy text requires either no material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion; the summary does not show that standard is met.
The model-card draft reportedly states there are no known material limitations even though reviewer comments question whether this limitation must be disclosed.
The actor relies on public governance guidance about monitoring and documentation, but that guidance does not substitute for the case-specific policy predicate required for certification.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable under the governing policy despite the unresolved disclosure issue and incomplete mitigation record.
That the identified mitigation path is sufficient for certification, when the summary itself says key required mitigation fields remain TBD.
Any implication that aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents cure a disclosure-policy failure for a named launch use case.
